Inclusion is borderline and rests on the published detector paper (arXiv:1708.00101), which names LNGS as the planned host and calls the device a dark matter detector; no dark matter result exists and the underground phase is only reported in a 2021 paper on fast-neutron detection. Tier C.
The 2014 contribution planned a 40 kg detector at Milano-Bicocca to be operated at LNGS in 2015; nothing read confirms that.

summary.plain: MOSCAB (Materia OSCura A Bolle, 'dark matter with bubbles') was a bubble chamber of superheated fluorine-rich liquid, built to look for dark matter and tested at Milano-Bicocca and then at Gran Sasso. No dark matter result was published; in 2021 the equipment was reported as used to detect fast neutrons.
summary.technical: Geyser-concept bubble chamber: a closed quartz vessel holding a target liquid (octafluoropropane C3F8) and its vapour, separated by a buffer liquid, in a thermal bath; designed for spin-dependent WIMP-proton sensitivity. Surface tests with 0.7 L of C3F8, then a 2 L scale-up (56 test runs, about 400 h, May-June 2017); underground at LNGS with a 2 L vessel (1.2 L C3F8) and an 18 L vessel (13 L C3F8).
